title: Agent Archivist exact-inference artifact (inference_artifact_version 1)
description: The durable record for one exact-inference capture (plan Phase 9; CAP-008): one artifact per observed provider-boundary event — a decoded provider request, a decoded provider response, one ordered decoded streaming event, a retry decision, a usage report, or a transport error. Bytes are captured at the proxy/SDK hook boundary AFTER HTTP transfer decoding: request and response payload bytes are the transferred content, never TLS/TCP framing, never transfer-encoding framing. Every field the HTTP boundary exposed travels only inside the closed `metadata` allowlist (content type, provider request ID, HTTP status, rate-limit metadata, usage counters); the record's own members are archivist-constructed provenance. The record always excludes authorization, cookies, and provider credentials by name (the reserved list), and it never carries TLS framing or a storage-location name: content is referenced by digest only. Correlation identifiers (`trace_id`, `inference_request_id`, `provider_attempt_id`) join attempts to the expected-inference ledger and to orchestrator attempts and are never inputs to any digest or storage key — the payload digest is the plain SHA-256 of the captured bytes and nothing else (plan Phase 9: joined 'without putting any of them in the blob identity'). Captured once at the boundary, the record is byte-stable: an upload retry of a spooled artifact rewrites identical bytes rather than adding a second record.

x-archivist.captureBoundary: plan Phase 9: payload bytes are captured at the proxy/SDK hook boundary after HTTP transfer decoding — never TLS/TCP framing, never transfer-encoding framing; a failure below the decoded-content boundary is a transport-error record carrying an error class, never framing bytes
x-archivist.blobIdentity: content-addressed: the payload digest is the plain SHA-256 of the captured bytes (the one label-less digest, per schemas/v1/ingest-identifiers.json). trace_id, inference_request_id, provider_attempt_id, and every other correlation or provenance field are record members only and are never inputs to any digest or storage key (plan Phase 9 correlation rule)
x-archivist.metadataAllowlist: closed: `metadata` rejects every name outside the allowlist outright. A new metadata entry is a new schema major (v2), never an additive v1 field — the closure is the boundary that keeps header and body material from drifting into archive metadata (plan Section 11: provider credentials must never become archive metadata)

inference_artifact_version.description: Exact-inference artifact schema major version (plan Section 7.1 version axis; this family's own axis, independent of occurrence/attestation/episode versions). Integer, currently 1; readers retain old-version support. New optional record members land inside v1; new required members, redefined members, a new `metadata` allowlist entry, a new closed-enum value, or changed correlation rules require v2.

artifact_kind.description: Which provider-boundary event this record is (plan Phase 9 artifact kinds, in the plan's order). `provider-request` and `provider-response` carry one decoded HTTP body each; `streaming-event` carries one ordered decoded event of a streamed attempt; `retry` records that a further transport attempt was started and why; `usage` carries the bounded usage counters the boundary extracted from a response body or stream event; `transport-error` records a failure that produced no decodable provider response. Identity-bearing: the kind is the interpretive frame for every other member, so an unknown value fails closed.

tenant_id.description: Issuer-created tenant identifier (plan Section 7.4), same grammar and scoping role as in the raw provenance family: exact-inference capture lives inside the tenant's archive, and cross-tenant writes are denied before any storage key is derived (SEC-003).

origin_client_id.description: The linked installation whose proxy or SDK hook captured the boundary (plan Phase 9 hook route). Capture provenance, not upload provenance: who later presents the spooled artifact for ingest is wire material and never rewrites this field.

trace_id.description: UUIDv7 identifier of the orchestrator operation (plan Phase 9). Correlation only: never an input to any digest or storage key.

inference_request_id.description: UUIDv7 identifier of the logical inference — one orchestrator request that may span several transport attempts (plan Phase 9). Groups this artifact with its siblings; the expected-inference ledger (plan Phase 9) freezes the matching expectation before route selection. Correlation only: never an input to any digest or storage key.

provider_attempt_id.description: UUIDv7 identifier of the one transport attempt this artifact belongs to (plan Phase 9: one per transport attempt). Every artifact of an attempt shares it, so retry and stream ordering are reconstructable without merging two provider attempts. Correlation only: never an input to any digest or storage key.

attempt_ordinal.description: Zero-based ordinal of the transport attempt within the logical inference, dense and increasing (attempt 0 is the first wire attempt). Reconstructs retry order even when UUIDv7 clocks are unreadable; `provider_attempt_id` remains the identity. Correlation only.

capture_time.description: Optional UTC time the boundary captured these bytes (plan Section 5 timing rule: RFC 3339 UTC, local time is a display choice). Omitted — never null — when the boundary cannot clock the event, e.g. a transport error with no readable monotonic-to-wall mapping. Frozen at capture, so an upload retry reproduces identical bytes.

payload_digest.description: SHA-256 of the captured payload bytes — the decoded content exactly as the boundary saw it, one byte per byte. The one label-less digest (a plain content digest, per schemas/v1/ingest-identifiers.json): identical bytes deduplicate to one stored blob, and no correlation field is folded in.

payload_size.description: Size in bytes of the captured payload, at least 1: the member is present only when at least one byte was captured, so an empty body is the member's absence, never a zero entry.

payload.description: The captured bytes, when any were: the decoded request body (`provider-request`), the decoded response body (`provider-response`), one decoded stream event (`streaming-event`), or the bytes of the event that reported usage (`usage`, optional). Absent for `retry` and for `transport-error` unless partial bytes were captured before the failure (e.g. a stream interrupted mid-body). Carries the bytes by digest and size only — never a storage location (the reserved list rejects those names; the storage layout is decided with the normative protocol contract, not here).

content_type.description: Media type the boundary observed for these bytes (request Content-Type or response Content-Type), retained verbatim including parameters. Printable ASCII, at most 256 bytes, no control characters.

provider_request_id.description: The provider's own request identifier as the boundary observed it (for example an `x-request-id`-style response header). Printed opaque: bounded printable ASCII, retained verbatim, never matched against a grammar the provider did not declare.

http_status.description: HTTP status code of the response, when a response status line was decoded. Transport outcome metadata: required to interpret rate-limit metadata and retry decisions, and never provider content (the response body is the `provider-response` artifact's payload, not here).

rate_limit_limit.description: Provider rate-limit window allowance, as a non-negative integer, normalized from the boundary's rate-limit metadata (the `limit` half of the IETF ratelimit headers and their provider-specific equivalents). Values the provider does not report as integers stay out of the archive; the raw bytes, when captured, remain in the payload.

rate_limit_remaining.description: Provider rate-limit remaining allowance, normalized as `rate_limit_limit` is.

rate_limit_reset.description: Provider rate-limit reset metadata, normalized as a non-negative integer. Providers disagree on the unit (seconds-until-reset versus epoch seconds); the value is retained exactly as reported and its unit is interpreted downstream from the declared route policy in the expected-inference ledger, never guessed here.

usage_input_tokens.description: Input token count the boundary extracted from the usage report. The bounded intersection all supported providers expose; provider-specific usage detail stays in the payload bytes. Required for the `usage` kind and optional nowhere else.

usage_output_tokens.description: Output token count, normalized as `usage_input_tokens` is.

usage_total_tokens.description: Total token count as reported. Retained as reported rather than recomputed, so a provider's own arithmetic (cached or discounted tokens) is never silently rewritten; input plus output at most total is a producer invariant, validated downstream (VAL-002), not schema syntax.

metadata.description: The closed metadata allowlist (plan Phase 9: an allowlist of content-type, provider request ID, rate-limit, and usage metadata). The only closed object in this family: `additionalProperties` is false, so every header-derived value the boundary did not normalize into a listed entry is excluded outright — authorization, cookies, and provider credentials cannot appear here even as future additive fields, because growth of the allowlist is a new schema major. Present when at least one allowlisted value was observed; omitted — never empty and never null — when none were.

event_ordinal.description: Zero-based dense ordinal of this event within its attempt's decoded stream (`streaming-event` only): events of one `provider_attempt_id`, ordered by `event_ordinal`, concatenate byte-for-byte to the attempt's decoded response body. Required for `streaming-event`, absent otherwise.

retry_of_attempt_ordinal.description: The `attempt_ordinal` of the attempt this retry follows (`retry` only): strictly less than this record's own `attempt_ordinal`, and the attempt it names must exist within the same `inference_request_id`. Required for `retry`, absent otherwise.

retry_reason.description: Why the retry was started (`retry` only), classified at the boundary: `http-status` (a decoded error status not classified as rate limiting), `rate-limit` (a decoded rate-limit rejection), `transport-error` (the prior attempt ended in a transport-error record), `stream-incomplete` (the stream ended before a terminal event), `timeout` (a deadline the boundary enforces). Provenance classification, not provider content: an unknown value fails closed. Required for `retry`, absent otherwise.

backoff_ms.description: Optional delay in milliseconds the boundary observed between the failed attempt and the retried one (`retry` only). Bounded wall-duration, not a monotonic-clock duration: the monotonic rule (plan Section 5) governs client retry budgets at the wire, while this value records the observed spacing for reconstruction.

usage_source.description: Where the usage counters were extracted from (`usage` only): `response-body` (the decoded body of a non-streamed response) or `stream-event` (one decoded event of a streamed attempt). When the source was a stream event, the `payload` member, when present, carries the reporting event's own digest, so the event is identified by matching `payload_digest` within the attempt's streaming-event artifacts. Required for `usage`, absent otherwise.

error_class.description: Closed transport-failure classification (`transport-error` only): `connect` (TCP connect failed), `dns` (resolution failed), `tls-handshake` (the handshake failed — the class names the layer of failure; the record still carries no TLS framing bytes), `read-timeout`, `write-timeout`, `connection-reset`, `stream-interrupted` (the decoded stream ended abnormally), `transfer-decode` (the declared transfer or content encoding did not decode), `other` (a counted residual for a failure the boundary could not classify — the archive counts it rather than inventing a detail). No free-text detail member exists: error strings are a known credential-leak route (plan Section 11), so a v2 with an explicit scrubbing rule is the only path to detail. Required for `transport-error`, absent otherwise.

timeout_ms.description: Optional deadline in milliseconds for a timeout-classified transport error (`transport-error` only).
